## Objective and scope

Compare the rank-one update with a simple consistent regularized descent baseline under the same objective, initialization, grid and resource envelope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Run the bounded predeclared lanes; report anatomy, objective components, geometry, accepted/rejected steps, support, runtime and memory rather than accepted-step count alone.
2. Introduce scale-aware convergence/stall criteria based on meaningful objective progress and physical step size, with explicit iteration-cap termination. Demonstrate reproducibility and bounded failure behavior.
3. Add a more elaborate solver only if the simple baseline identifies a measured need; a CC curvature model requires explicit validated mathematics.
4. Publish a numerical baseline decision, including negative anatomy outcomes. Selecting a numerically coherent baseline completes this experiment but cannot pass G4 without anatomical gains.

## Planned areas

- modules/reframe4s-halfflow/shared/src/main/scala/reframe4s/halfflow/HalfFlowCcControl.scala
- modules/reframe4s-halfflow/shared/src/main/scala/reframe4s/halfflow/HalfFlowCcEngine.scala
- benchmarks/flashalign/
- docs/benchmarks/

## Blocking prerequisites

- O01 (`bd-01M4X4DYQT456CQJT20F7633HN`)

## Evidence and safeguards

Use Mote claims/path reservations when implementation begins. Preserve unrelated dirty work and immutable historical studies. Reuse canonical providers and current owners. Keep labels/evaluation-only masks out of fitting, tuning on qualification data, and runtime stopping. Record exact source/provider/input/config identities, commands, numerical tolerances and all failures; run affected JVM/Scala.js and independent numerical checks. Current geometry/export thresholds cannot be relaxed to improve a pass rate. Completed research may be negative; milestone/epic acceptance remains a separate evidence-based decision.
